focus: /ʌ/ (money, much) vs /ɒ/ (shop, cost) · /aɪ/ (buy, price) vs /eɪ/ (pay) · rising vs falling intonation in questions · prices: -teen vs -ty again · /ʃ/ (shop) vs /s/ (size)
focus_ar: /ʌ/ مقابل /ɒ/، و /aɪ/ مقابل /eɪ/، ونغمة السؤال الصاعدة والهابطة، والأسعار، و /ʃ/ مقابل /s/
arabic_challenge: /ʌ/ has no direct Arabic equivalent and is often replaced by /a/ or /o/. Intonation is the big one this week: Arabic question intonation differs, and a flat 'How much is it?' can sound abrupt or unclear to an English ear.

isolation.instructions: /ʌ/ (money, much, some) = short, central, relaxed — a quick grunt with the mouth barely open. /ɒ/ (shop, cost, not) = rounder lips, tongue further back and lower.
isolation.instructions_ar: /ʌ/ قصير ومركزي والفم مفتوح شوية صغيرة. /ɒ/ الشفاه مدوّرة أكثر واللسان لورا وتحت.

daily_drills.record_this: How much money do you have? It costs one hundred pounds. The shop is not open, so some customers are waiting.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'cup' then 'cop'. Are your lips rounder for the second one?

isolation.instructions: /aɪ/ (buy, price, five) starts wide open and glides to /ɪ/. /eɪ/ (pay, eight) starts half open and glides to /ɪ/. Both move upward, but /aɪ/ starts much lower.
isolation.instructions_ar: /aɪ/ يبدأ مفتوح جدًا ويتحرك لأعلى. /eɪ/ يبدأ نص مفتوح ويتحرك لأعلى. الاتنين متحركين لكن /aɪ/ يبدأ أوطى.

sentence_practice: What is the price? I will pay.
daily_drills.record_this: I want to buy five, please. What is the price? I will pay now and take the change later.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'buy' and 'bay'. The first should start with your mouth clearly wider open.

isolation.instructions: Yes/No questions RISE at the end: 'Do you have this?↗' Wh- questions FALL at the end: 'How much is it?↘' Getting this backwards sounds unnatural or even rude.
isolation.instructions_ar: أسئلة نعم/لا نغمتها صاعدة في الآخر ↗. وأسئلة (how/what/where) نغمتها هابطة ↘. العكس بيبقى غريب أو جاف.
practice: Do you have it? ↗ (voice goes UP)
How much is it? ↘ (voice goes DOWN)

sentence_practice: Do you have a bigger size? ↗
daily_drills.record_this: How much is it? Do you have a bigger size? Can I pay by card, or do you accept only cash?
daily_drills.self_check: Hum the tune of each question without words. Does the yes/no one rise and the wh- one fall?

isolation.instructions: This week the -teen/-ty difference costs real money. fifTEEN pounds (15) vs FIFty pounds (50). Stress the last syllable for -teen, the first for -ty, and keep the -ty ending short.
isolation.instructions_ar: الفرق بين -teen و -ty هنا بيغيّر السعر. fifTEEN (١٥) مقابل FIFty (٥٠). النبر على الآخر في -teen وعلى الأول في -ty.

daily_drills.record_this: It costs fifteen pounds, not fifty. I only have thirty pounds with me. The total is forty-five, and the shirt was nineteen.
daily_drills.self_check: Say a price and have someone write it. Did they write the number you meant?

isolation.instructions: /ʃ/ (shop, cash) = tongue pulled back, lips slightly rounded, a full 'shhh'. /s/ (size, cost) = tongue forward behind the teeth, a thin, sharp hiss.
isolation.instructions_ar: /ʃ/ اللسان لورا والشفاه مدوّرة شوية (شhhh). /s/ اللسان لقدام خلف الأسنان وصفير رقيق حاد.

sentence_practice: I go shopping for shoes and shirts.
I will pay cash at the shop.
daily_drills.record_this: I go shopping for shoes and shirts. What size is this, and what is the price? I will pay cash at the shop and save some money.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'she' then 'see'. Are your lips rounded for the first and spread for the second?

challenge_sentences: How much money do you have? ↘
Do you have this in a bigger size? ↗
It costs fifteen pounds, not fifty.
I go shopping and pay cash.
daily_drills.record_this: How much money do you have? Do you have this shirt in a bigger size? It costs fifteen pounds, not fifty. I go shopping every week and I always pay cash.
daily_drills.self_check: Check the intonation: does every yes/no question rise and every wh- question fall?

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself acting out a shopping conversation. Then listen back and check each sound group.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك وانت تعمل حوار شراء، وبعدين اسمع وراجع كل مجموعة أصوات.
test_yourself.passage: Excuse me, how much is this shirt? Fifteen pounds? Not fifty? That is cheap. Do you have it in a bigger size? I like this colour. I want to buy two, please. Can I pay by card, or do you accept only cash? Here is one hundred pounds. How much change do I get? Thank you very much. The shop is nice and the prices are good.

sounds_to_check./ʌ/ vs /ɒ/: much, money, hundred, colour — shop, not, cost, dollar
sounds_to_check./aɪ/ vs /eɪ/: buy, price, size, like, five, nine — pay, eight, sale, change
sounds_to_check.intonation: How much is this?↘  Do you have it?↗  Can I pay by card?↗
sounds_to_check.-teen vs -ty: fifTEEN vs FIFty, thirTEEN vs THIRty
sounds_to_check./ʃ/ vs /s/: shirt, shop, cash, shopping — size, sale, cost, price

scoring_guide.90_100: Prices are unambiguous and question tunes are natural. Ready for week 8.
scoring_guide.50_69: 15/50 confusion, or all questions on one flat tune. Repeat days 3-4.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5, humming the question tunes before adding words.

for_arabic_speakers: Intonation carries politeness in English. A flat question can sound abrupt even when every sound is correct.
/ʌ/ is not /a/ and not /o/ — it is short, central and relaxed.
The -teen/-ty stress difference is a money risk. Over-emphasise it when shopping.
Keep /ʃ/ and /s/ distinct: 'she sells' should have two clearly different hisses.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
